chunks: Saad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Suwayd al-Qalla' from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who forgets and prays four rak'at during travel. He said: 'If he remembered on that day, he should repeat [the prayer]; but if he did not remember until that day passed, there is no need for him to repeat [it].'
Thus, this report is interpreted as indicating a type of recommended act (istihbab), while the first case [remembering on the same day] is interpreted as indicating obligation (wujub).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who forgets and prays four rak'at instead of two?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the validity of *Qasr* prayer for a traveler who forgets to shorten it, distinguishing between immediate recall and delayed memory. The scholar notes that the requirement to repeat is obligatory (*wajib*) if remembered the same day, whereas the exemption after the day passes is considered recommended (*mustahabb*), reflecting the principle of ease in travel. This highlights the nuanced application of *rukhsah* (concession) in Shia jurisprudence regarding forgotten acts of worship.
